Peter and Paul

Icons

Sts. Peter and Paul

The Chief Apostles · Sts. Peter and Paul of Belozersk

What is depictedHistory and traditionPublished explanationSources

Scripture

Matthew 16:15–19

2 Timothy 4:6–8

King James Version · Scripture previews

The Belozersk icon places Sts. Peter and Paul side by side as full-length figures. The old panel is identified with the Novgorod school.

[1] Displayed work;file-level title,description,date and visual identification

What is depicted

Both apostles hold books or scrolls and turn slightly towards the centre. The contrasting hair, beard and garments distinguish the paired figures. Their halos and inscriptions identify them within the named historical work; this is not a group portrait of the entire apostolic company.

[1] Displayed work;file-level title,description,date and visual identification

History and tradition

The file dates the work to the twelfth–thirteenth centuries and locates its provenance at Belozersk. This object history is distinct from the apostles’ first-century lives. The readings below preserve separate Gospel and Pauline voices instead of combining their words into one invented speech.

[1] Displayed work;file-level title,description,date and visual identification

Published explanation

He saith unto them, But whom say ye that I am?

And Simon Peter answered and said, Thou art the Christ, the Son of the living God.

And Jesus answered and said unto him, Blessed art thou, Simon Bar-jona: for flesh and blood hath not revealed it unto thee, but my Father which is in heaven.

And I say also unto thee, That thou art Peter, and upon this rock I will build my church; and the gates of hell shall not prevail against it.

And I will give unto thee the keys of the kingdom of heaven: and whatsoever thou shalt bind on earth shall be bound in heaven: and whatsoever thou shalt loose on earth shall be loosed in heaven.

Canonical scriptural narrative in the identified historical English edition; later biographical traditions are separately attributed.

[2] Matthew 16:15–19

For I am now ready to be offered, and the time of my departure is at hand.

I have fought a good fight, I have finished my course, I have kept the faith:

Henceforth there is laid up for me a crown of righteousness, which the Lord, the righteous judge, shall give me at that day: and not to me only, but unto all them also that love his appearing.

Canonical scriptural narrative in the identified historical English edition; later biographical traditions are separately attributed.
